items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: Willy Smith was one of the most warmest guys and Joe Thomas, and some of them, you know

ctx.x: Connecticut. And we came from Pittsburgh. Doggone, a long ride from Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania to Hartford, Connecticut. And we were so tired. Gee whiz.

Basie said, "Well, I'm tired like everybody else, you know." And most of the guys in Jimmy Lunceford's band didn't even speak. Willy Smith was one of the most warmest guys and Joe Thomas, and some of them, you know -- here Count Basie, we got out of the bus, was ragged, you know. But we got on the bandstand, we started popping. We started shying down. Dolgarn, before you know it, Jimmy Lunceford was coming up to the bandstand. All the guys was coming up, you know. So we put a hurting on him that night. Oh, we…
Well, that's like, you know, Harry Carney says the only band that washed Duke's band out was Fletcher Henderson's and he said that was when they let Coleman Hawkins play practically all night.
